title: JavaBench: A Benchmark of Object-Oriented Code Generation for Evaluating Large Language Models.
verified_bounded_claim: The paper's census of 24 code-generation benchmarks found a strong Python and function-level concentration and motivated class- and project-level object-oriented evaluation.
verification_note: JavaBench itself evaluates Java object-oriented method generation; the census and benchmark results should retain their sampled-benchmark, language, task, and model boundaries.

title: An Agent-based Evaluation Framework for Complex Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: The proposed framework reported higher Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlations with human-annotated scores than the three evaluated baselines.
verification_note: The arXiv record and PDF metadata retain the earlier CodeVisionary title, while the visible first-page title is An Agent-based Evaluation Framework for Complex Code Generation. The study evaluates 363 samples across 37 scenarios and 23 languages; verify final-version wording and counts before citing details unique to the DOI article.

title: Code-DiTing: Automatic Evaluation of Code Generation without References or Test Cases.
verified_bounded_claim: The comparison exposes tradeoffs among judge accuracy, prompt complexity, explanation quality, and computational demand; the proposed distilled judges are evaluated as one bounded alternative.
verification_note: The accessible preprint uses the title CODE-DITING: A Reasoning-Based Metric for Functional Alignment in Code Evaluation and three judge datasets; verify final-version terminology before DOI-specific use.

title: RealisticCodeBench: Towards More Realistic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: Tasks mined from code marked as generated by ChatGPT or Copilot produce a workload distinct from algorithmic suites and deliberately target code that developers used assistants to attempt.
verification_note: The benchmark contains 376 source problems translated across five languages and evaluates 12 models; repository tags are evidence of attributed use, not a representative sample of every developer workload.

title: CoderEval: A Benchmark of Pragmatic Code Generation with Generative Pre-trained Models.
verified_bounded_claim: In the sampled popular repositories, non-standalone functions exceeded 70 percent, and the evaluated models performed substantially better on standalone than context-dependent tasks.
verification_note: The accepted-manuscript artifact is matched by title and authors to DOI 10.1145/3597503.3623316, but its embedded DOI is erroneously 10.1145/3597503.3623322, which identifies a different paper. Do not represent these bytes as the published ACM version. CoderEval covers 230 Python and 230 Java tasks with six context-dependency levels; the repository sample and tested models bound the results.

title: HumanEvo: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for More Realistic Evaluation of Repository-Level Code Generation.
verified_bounded_claim: Repository-level evaluation can leak later project state when it supplies the latest context instead of the context available when the target function was created; HumanEvo measures that evolution boundary.
verification_note: The arXiv record identifies this version as accepted for ICSE 2025. The reported inflation range depends on HumanEvo, seven evaluated models, and the studied context-acquisition methods; it is not a universal correction factor.

title: Benchmarking Automated Program Repair: An Extensive Study on Both Real-World and Artificial Bugs.
verified_bounded_claim: A common environment, real and mutation-derived bugs, and multiple outcome dimensions exposed complementary behavior and implementation issues that aggregate fixed-bug counts would conceal.
verification_note: The study compares nine learning-based and three traditional tools on Defects4J and a 1700-bug MuBench; its tool, language, benchmark, and metric choices bound the findings.

title: HumanEvalComm: Benchmarking the Communication Competence of Code Generation for LLMs and LLM Agents.
verified_bounded_claim: Communication evaluation separately measures whether systems ask useful clarifying questions when requirements are inconsistent, ambiguous, or incomplete before scoring resulting code.
verification_note: The DBLP title uses the plural LLM Agents, while the preserved PDF, arXiv record, and Crossref title use the singular LLM Agent. HumanEvalComm is a manually modified benchmark with an LLM-based question evaluator and specified models; its communication and code metrics are not independent human-quality judgments.

title: LLM-Based Test-Driven Interactive Code Generation: User Study and Empirical Evaluation.
verified_bounded_claim: In a 15-programmer study, test-guided interaction improved code evaluation and reduced reported cognitive load without a statistically significant completion-time increase; simulated scaling used an idealized user proxy.
verification_note: The human study used bounded tasks and participants, while the four-model benchmark experiment substituted reference behavior for live user feedback; keep those evidence modes separate.

title: Biases and differences in code review using medical imaging and eye-tracking: genders, humans, and machines.
verified_bounded_claim: With code quality controlled, reviewer behavior and attention differed with participant gender and the pull request's apparent author, showing that a human checkpoint is not automatically an unbiased oracle.
verification_note: The controlled study used 37 participants, 60 pull requests, and three apparent-author conditions; it supports the existence of effects in that design, not universal effect sizes.

title: A Systematic Literature Review on the Use of Deep Learning in Software Engineering Research.
verified_bounded_claim: The review organizes 128 studies across 23 software-engineering tasks around learning components, including data, model, training, evaluation, and reproducibility considerations.
verification_note: This is a secondary synthesis with stated search, extraction, and reproducibility-assessment limits; use it to frame reporting dimensions rather than as direct evidence that a particular agent protocol works.

title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
verified_bounded_claim: The review spans heterogeneous software-engineering tasks and separately analyzes model use, data preparation, optimization and evaluation, and task applications, supporting an explicit scope boundary for this monograph.
verification_note: The accessible author copy is an earlier 229-paper, 2017-2023 version with placeholder publication metadata; the DOI article reports a later 395-paper corpus, so do not transfer counts across versions.

title: Machine/Deep Learning for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review.
verified_bounded_claim: Across its 1428-paper corpus, the review treats data preparation, representation, model design and training, evaluation, and rationale reporting as conditions of reproducibility and replicability.
verification_note: This is a broad 2009-2020 secondary review of ML/DL software-engineering studies; its reporting findings motivate methods disclosure but do not validate coding-agent effectiveness.
